title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. However, existing methods often model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately, while directly incorporating predicted futures into action policies without sufficiently considering their relevance to current action requirements. To address these limitations, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval. Specifically, Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones, and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), establishing dependencies across temporal horizons. Building upon these predictions, Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to facilitate fine-grained retrieval. Furthermore, Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval adaptively retrieves relevant future information from the structured latent world based on evolving action representations during denoising, providing targeted guidance for action generation. Extensive experiments on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.
full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. However, existing methods often model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately, while directly incorporating predicted futures into action policies without sufficiently considering their relevance to current action requirements. To address these limitations, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval. Specifically, Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones, and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), establishing dependencies across temporal horizons. Building upon these predictions, Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to facilitate fine-grained retrieval. Furthermore, Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval adaptively retrieves relevant future information from the structured latent world based on evolving action representations during denoising, providing targeted guidance for action generation. Extensive experiments on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. Introduction sec:intro Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models~ kim2024openvla,intelligence2025pi_,yang2026eventvla,zheng2026xvla,shi2026memoryvla,luo2026being,zhu2026ati,liu2026plaw have achieved remarkable progress in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation within a unified end-to-end framework. Benefiting from advances in large-scale vision-language models and the growing availability of diverse robotic demonstrations, recent VLA models have demonstrated promising capabilities across a wide range of manipulation tasks. As robotic manipulation tasks become increasingly complex, anticipating future environmental changes and task evolution becomes essential for effective action generation. To this end, recent studies have explored incorporating foresight capabilities into VLA models to enhance their understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression~ liu2026last,kim2026cosmos,xiao2026rehearsevla . Existing approaches primarily predict future states or latent representations to model environmental dynamics~ liu2026last,nguyen2026foca,zhang2026dreamvla,zheng2025flare,huang2025ladi , or generate future images and videos to anticipate visual scene evolution~ zhang2026foreact,kim2026cosmos,xiao2026rehearsevla,shen2026videovla,bu2024closed , thereby providing additional foresight information for action generation. Despite these advances, effectively translating future predictions into actionable guidance for complex robotic manipulation remains challenging. First, modeling short-term world dynamics or long-term task objectives in isolation limits hierarchical coordination across temporal horizons. As illustrated in Fig.~ fig:motivation (a), many existing foresight-based VLA methods primarily focus on a single prediction horizon. Short-term prediction methods~ zhong2025flowvla,cen2025worldvla,yang2026mantis,li2026fomovla emphasize near-future environmental changes and local motion dynamics, capturing fine-grained state evolution but often lacking explicit connections to subsequent task stages and ultimate goals. In contrast, long-term prediction methods~ zhang2026foreact,chen2026goal,zhao2025cot,shou2026halo,long2026scaling provide intermediate task guidance through semantic subtask planning or visual subgoal prediction, enabling the policy to anticipate key future task states. However, these methods often lack sufficient modeling of the continuous state transitions and motion dynamics required to achieve such objectives. Although both forms of foresight provide valuable information, modeling them independently makes it difficult to establish explicit dependencies among local state evolution, key semantic milestones, and final task objectives, thereby limiting the policy's coherent understanding of task progression across temporal horizons. More importantly, directly incorporating predicted future information into action generation often overlooks its varying relevance to current action requirements. As illustrated in Fig.~ fig:motivation (a), many existing approaches~ zhong2025flowvla,cen2025worldvla,yang2026mantis,zhang2026foreact,chen2026goal,zhao2025cot,wang2026wave directly incorporate predicted future images or latent representations into action policies as additional conditioning signals, without sufficiently distinguishing the relevance of different predictions to current actions. However, future information across different prediction horizons, camera views, and spatial regions contributes differently to action generation, and its relevance dynamically evolves throughout task execution and the action generation process. Therefore, even with rich and complementary future predictions, selectively retrieving and utilizing information relevant to current action requirements remains essential for fully exploiting the decision-making potential of foresight. These observations motivate a unified framework that establishes hierarchical dependencies across temporal horizons and adaptively retrieves and leverages relevant future information according to current action requirements. To address these challenges, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval for robotic manipulation. As illustrated in Fig.~ fig:motivation (b), HiFOR integrates multi-horizon foresight prediction with action-guided selective retrieval, enabling future information across different temporal horizons to provide targeted guidance according to evolving action requirements. Specifically, we first introduce , which jointly predicts short-term state evolution, key semantic milestones, and final goal states. By incorporating a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), the prediction module establishes asymmetric dependencies across temporal horizons, connecting local motion dynamics with intermediate task progression and long-term objectives. Building upon these predictions, we propose , which organizes predicted future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to construct a structured latent world while preserving fine-grained structural information for subsequent selective retrieval. Furthermore, we develop , which leverages evolving action representations during denoising to perform factorized attention over the structured latent world. By adaptively evaluating the relevance of different prediction horizons, camera views, and spatial regions to current actions, the retrieved future information provides targeted guidance for action generation. Through these designs, HiFOR effectively integrates hierarchical future modeling with action-guided information retrieval, enabling foresight predictions to better support robotic manipulation. Our main contributions are summarized as follows: First, we propose a hierarchical foresight prediction mechanism that jointly models short-term state evolution, key semantic milestones, and final goal states through hierarchical dependency modeling, establishing explicit connections between local world dynamics and long-term task objectives. Second, we develop an action-guided structured world retrieval mechanism that adaptively retrieves future information relevant to current action requirements from a structured latent world organized along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions through denoising-aware factorized attention. Third, we conduct extensive experiments on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks, demonstrating the effectiveness of HiFOR and further validating the contributions of its key components through comprehensive ablation studies. Related Works sec:formatting Vision-Language-Action Model sec:related_vla Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models aim to integrate visual perception, language understanding, and action generation to develop general-purpose robotic policies capable of executing complex manipulation tasks. Based on their action representations and generation mechanisms, existing VLA models can be broadly categorized into two paradigms: discrete and continuous action generation. Discrete action generation methods~ brohan2022rt,brohan2023rt, kim2024openvla,ye2025latent,zhao2025cot,pertsch2025fast, xu2026moeactok,liang2025discrete,yang2026chain convert continuous actions into discrete tokens or textual sequences, enabling autoregressive action prediction. In contrast, continuous action generation methods~ kim2025fine, black2024pi_0,intelligence2025pi_,li2026forcevla2,guo2026reflex typically employ specialized action prediction modules to directly generate continuous control signals, mainly adopting regression-based, diffusion-based, or flow-matching-based approaches. Specifically, regression-based methods~ kim2025fine,wu2024unleashing directly learn mappings from observations to actions, while diffusion-based methods~ liu2025rdt,wen2025diffusionvla,chuang2026lie,wen2025dexvla generate action sequences through iterative denoising. Flow-matching-based methods~ black2024pi_0,intelligence2025pi_, routray2026vipra,zuo2026delta,tang2026fewer,shin2026dual learn a continuous vector field to transform samples from a noise distribution into the target action distribution. Although these approaches have improved the action generation and generalization capabilities of VLA models, they primarily focus on action prediction itself, whereas accurate local action predictions do not necessarily guarantee successful completion of complex manipulation tasks. Foresight Predication in VLA To overcome the limitations of local action prediction, recent studies have incorporated foresight prediction into VLA to anticipate future environmental changes and task progression, thereby guiding action generation. Based on how future information is represented, existing methods can be categorized into implicit and explicit foresight prediction. Implicit methods~ liu2026last,nguyen2026foca,zhang2026dreamvla,zheng2025flare,huang2025ladi,yi2026placa model environmental dynamics in state or latent feature spaces, leveraging predicted future representations to facilitate policy learning and action generation. In contrast, explicit methods~ zhang2026foreact,kim2026cosmos,xiao2026rehearsevla,shen2026videovla,bu2024closed,cen2025rynnvla generate future images or videos to anticipate visual scene evolution and potential action outcomes, supporting robotic planning and decision-making. Despite these advances, existing methods still face limitations in modeling and utilizing future information. First, predicting short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives in isolation overlooks dependencies across temporal horizons, limiting coherent modeling of task progression. Second, existing methods often directly incorporate predicted future information into action policies as additional conditioning signals, without adequately considering its varying relevance to current action requirements. title: Cheap Retrieval and Observation Credit Assignment from One Quantity: The Value of Information
comment: 11 pages, 1 figure. Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Memory for Robot Foundation Models (https://corl2026-memory.github.io/)
summary: Memory in reinforcement learning raises two problems. Attention finds the relevant item by scoring the whole store, which is costly for robots under latency and energy limits. When a retrieved memory pays off, credit for acquiring it must cross the whole sequence. We argue that both are governed by one quantity, the value of information, and propose to estimate it from archived rollouts with a learned world model. We obtain that, when read at the observation, it yields a provable lower bound on the optimal value of the acquiring action, which floors its TD target and attributes this floor to the observation that earned it. Read at the decision, it defines the optimal retrieval set. A pilot retrieval system, to be trained and improved with this signal, solves a memory task with reduced context.

title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies
comment: Accepted at CoRL 2026. Project website: https://rlinf.github.io/LaWAM/
summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) leverage large-scale vision-language pretraining for semantic robot control, but often lack explicit foresight into how robot actions change the scene. World-Action Models (WAMs) address this limitation by conditioning policies on predicted futures, yet existing approaches typically rely on computationally expensive video generation with substantial pixel-level redundancy. We present LaWAM, a Latent World Action Model that exposes predictive dynamics to robot policies through compact latent visual subgoals instead of reconstructed future video. At the core of LaWAM is a latent-action-conditioned Latent World Model (LaWM). We obtain LaWM by training a latent action model in the latent space of a pretrained vision foundation model and repurposing its forward decoder to predict future observation features for scene evolution. LaWAM then conditions action generation on these predicted latent visual subgoals to enable dynamics-aware robot control. LaWAM achieves state-of-the-art or competitive success rates (SRs) across LIBERO (98.6% SR), RoboTwin (91.22% SR), and real-world manipulation tasks while retaining low-latency inference. LaWAM runs in 187 ms per action-chunk prediction and achieves up to 24x lower wall-clock latency than pixel-space WAMs.
full_text: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) leverage large-scale vision-language pretraining for semantic robot control, but often lack explicit foresight into how robot actions change the scene. World-Action Models (WAMs) address this limitation by conditioning policies on predicted futures, yet existing approaches typically rely on computationally expensive video generation with substantial pixel-level redundancy. We present , a Latent World Action Model that exposes predictive dynamics to robot policies through compact latent visual subgoals instead of reconstructed future video. At the core of LaWAM is a latent-action-conditioned Latent World Model (LaWM). We obtain LaWM by training a latent action model on features from a pretrained vision foundation model and repurposing its forward decoder to predict future observation features. LaWAM then conditions action generation on these predicted latent visual subgoals to enable dynamics-aware robot control. LaWAM achieves state-of-the-art or competitive success rates (SRs) across LIBERO (98.6 SR), RoboTwin (91.22 SR), and real-world manipulation tasks while retaining low-latency inference. LaWAM runs in 187\,ms per action-chunk prediction and achieves up to lower wall-clock latency than pixel-space WAMs. Project website: . Introduction r 0.48 fig:libero_latency Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) kim2024openvlaopensourcevisionlanguageactionmodel, kimOpenVLAOFTFinetuningVisionlanguageaction2025,https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2410.24164, geminiroboticsteam2025geminiroboticsbringingai, gr00tn1_2025 have recently shown strong performance on robotic manipulation by transferring large-scale vision-language pretraining into action generation. However, most current VLAs predict actions primarily from the current visual-language context, without explicitly modeling how the scene evolves under candidate actions mantisVersatileVisionlanguageaction2025, dialDecouplingIntentAction2026 . World-Action Models (WAMs) mimicvideoVideoactionModels2025, kim2026cosmospolicyfinetuningvideo, bi2025motusunifiedlatentaction, ye2026gigaworldpolicyefficientactioncenteredworldaction,li2026causalworldmodelingrobot, ye2026worldactionmodelszeroshot, lv2025f1visionlanguageactionmodelbridging offer a natural way to introduce temporal dynamics by augmenting policies with predicted future observations or states as additional context. However, current WAMs remain inefficient for manipulation policies. First, many methods predict future images or videos, allocating substantial modeling capacity to pixel-level synthesis rather than compact action-relevant dynamics. Second, iterative future generation introduces considerable inference latency; under the same evaluation setup used in Fig.~ fig:libero_latency , LingBot-VA li2026causalworldmodelingrobot requires 4482\,ms for a single policy inference, whereas the representative VLA intelligence2025pi05visionlanguageactionmodelopenworld requires only 220\,ms. Third, effective future prediction for manipulation should expose the state change relevant to the next action chunk, rather than merely generating visually plausible task-consistent futures. To address these limitations, we propose a Latent World Model (LaWM) for WAMs that predicts compact latent visual subgoals directly, rather than synthesizing future images or videos. LaWM is a latent-action-conditioned dynamics model that predicts future observation features corresponding to the scene change required for the next action chunk. By operating entirely in the latent space, LaWM models action-relevant dynamics efficiently without expensive or iterative pixel generation. We obtain LaWM by revisiting latent action models (LAMs) in the latent space of frozen visual encoders~ bruce2024geniegenerativeinteractiveenvironments , such as DINOv3~ simeoni2025dinov3 . A LAM contains an inverse-dynamics encoder that infers latent actions from visual transitions and a decoder that predicts the future latent state conditioned on the current latent state and latent action. Prior latent-action-based VLAs mainly use this framework to learn embodiment-agnostic action representations, treating the decoder only as an auxiliary training component and discarding it after pretraining schmidtLearningActActions2024, bruce2024geniegenerativeinteractiveenvironments, ye2025latentactionpretrainingvideos, yang2025learning . In contrast, we repurpose the decoder as the core predictive module of LaWM, using latent actions to generate future observation features that serve as latent visual subgoals for action generation. Building on this latent visual subgoal interface, we introduce the Latent World Action Model (LaWAM), which conditions action generation on LaWM-predicted future dynamics. Fig.~ fig:lawam provides an overview of the full two-stage pretraining pipeline. We first train LaWM as a latent-action-conditioned world model, then pretrain LaWAM with latent-action distillation for subgoal-conditioned action generation. Overall, the training pipeline uses roughly 3,000 hours of robot videos and 1,500 hours of egocentric human videos. At test time, the policy predicts a latent action, LaWM decodes it into a latent visual subgoal in a single forward pass, and an action expert generates the action chunk conditioned on both the current context and predicted subgoal. After benchmark-specific post-training, LaWAM achieves state-of-the-art or competitive success against strong VLA and WAM baselines on LIBERO~ liu2023libero , RoboTwin~ chen2025robotwin , and real-world manipulation, including long-horizon tasks and deformable-object manipulation, with 2.3B parameters. Beyond accuracy, Fig.~ fig:libero_latency shows that LaWAM combines non-iterative latent prediction with a compact 230M-parameter LaWM, using about 95 fewer world-modeling parameters than the 5B WAN backbone~ wan2025wanopenadvancedlargescale . LaWAM runs in 187\,ms per action-chunk prediction and achieves up to lower wall-clock latency than pixel-space WAMs. Related Work Vision-Language-Action Models. VLAs transfer large-scale vision-language pretraining into robot control, giving policies strong semantic grounding over instructions, objects, and task compositions kim2024openvlaopensourcevisionlanguageactionmodel, kimOpenVLAOFTFinetuningVisionlanguageaction2025, geminiroboticsteam2025geminiroboticsbringingai, gr00tn1_2025, lv2025f1visionlanguageactionmodelbridging, mantisVersatileVisionlanguageaction2025 . This semantic prior helps specify what the robot should achieve, but it does not by itself provide explicit reasoning about how the scene evolves under embodied interaction. Several recent VLAs adopt query-based designs to incorporate predictive information through learned queries and feature-alignment objectives zhengFLARERobotLearning2025, gr00tn1_2025, beingbeyond2026beingh07, su2026worldguidanceworldmodeling . For example, Mantis and VLA-JEPA use future prediction as auxiliary supervision~ mantisVersatileVisionlanguageaction2025,vlajepaEnhancingVisionlanguageaction2026 . LaWAM instead retains the forward decoder at inference and explicitly conditions action generation on its predicted spatial future; Appendix~ app:predictive_interfaces details this distinction. World-Action Models. World-Action Models (WAMs) jointly model future video and actions conditioned on observations and task instructions mimicvideoVideoactionModels2025, bi2025motusunifiedlatentaction, ye2026worldactionmodelszeroshot, kim2026cosmospolicyfinetuningvideo, li2026causalworldmodelingrobot, ye2026gigaworldpolicyefficientactioncenteredworldaction, fastwamNeedTesttimeFutureImagination2026 . Pixel-space WAMs provide explicit physical foresight through generated images or videos, but they inherit costly iterative generation and substantial appearance-level redundancy kim2026cosmospolicyfinetuningvideo, li2026causalworldmodelingrobot, jiang2026wovr . similarly conditions robot policies on visual subgoals, but these subgoals are produced by a separate iterative pixel-space model physicalIntelligencePi07Steerable2026 . Efficiency-oriented approaches such as Fast-WAM and Giga-World Policy reduce generation cost by making future prediction auxiliary or action-centered, which weakens the role of predicted dynamics as an explicit conditioning signal during test-time action generation~ fastwamNeedTesttimeFutureImagination2026,ye2026gigaworldpolicyefficientactioncenteredworldaction . Concurrent analyses likewise suggest that pretrained visual latent spaces provide stronger policy-facing dynamics representations than pixel-reconstruction spaces~ nilakshReconstructionSemantics2026 . While LDA-1B also models dynamics in a structured DINO latent space, it jointly denoises future visual states and action chunks through a diffusion-style process lyu2026lda1bscalinglatentdynamics . LaWAM jointly models future visual features and actions, representing the future by the endpoint of each fixed-physical-horizon action chunk. It decodes this latent visual subgoal in a single forward pass and directly conditions action generation on it at inference. Latent Action Models. Latent action models learn compact transition variables from unlabeled videos through latent inverse dynamics and forward prediction schmidtLearningActActions2024, bruce2024geniegenerativeinteractiveenvironments, ye2025latentactionpretrainingvideos, yang2025learning . Recent VLA and world-modeling methods use such variables as cross-embodiment action representations for policy learning and future prediction ye2025latentactionpretrainingvideos, bu2025univlalearningacttaskcentric, gaoAdaWorldLearningAdaptable2025, gao2026dreamdojogeneralistrobotworld . Most prior work focuses primarily on the latent action space itself---its discreteness or continuity, regularization, and downstream transfer. A complementary opportunity lies in the decoder: as concurrently observed by learningLatentActionWorldModelsWild2026 , the decoder of a latent action model already implements a latent action-conditioned world model. LaWAM builds on this observation by repurposing the decoder as a policy-facing latent dynamics interface, where latent actions are expanded into embodiment-grounded future observation features that directly condition action generation.
